MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JUNE 12, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
7:05 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR HUFF.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman*.
  *arrived at 7:15 p.m.
City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney’s Office Representative Kane Thugyen
  Planning Director David Wahha
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by
  a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  MAYOR HUFF requested that ITEMS 5D* and 5I* be removed for individual consideration
  and COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ requested that ITEM 5F* be removed for individual
  consideration. There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE REMAINING ITEMS AS PRESENTED
  BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JUNE 12, 2018
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the City
  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 22, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS –MAY 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 60017 THROUGH 60058 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $719,035.10 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 58540 (VOID); 59548 (VOID);
  050118 THROUGH 051118; 59999 THROUGH 59958; 59985 THROUGH 60016 IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $637,844.54 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $1,356,879.64
  WITH PROPER AUDIT.

E.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 21, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF JUNE 4, 2017

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  SEMI-ANNUAL CODE ENFORCEMENT REPORT – DECEMBER 1, 2017 THROUGH
  JUNE 1, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

* Items removed from Consent Calendar for individual consideration:

D.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 15, 2018

  In response to MAYOR HUFF regarding the schedule for the GPAC meetings,
  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ noted that thus far, the meeting are scheduled on an as
  needed basis based on the information that the consultant has to report from the
  research survey and other activities being conducted. Brief discussion ensued
  concerning the survey questions and how the survey was conducted specifically related
  to equestrian matters. Further discussion ensued concerning the trend toward other
  transportation means like ride-share and rental scooters; and the City’s housing needs.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY
  COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 15, 2018

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 12, 2018
 F.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 29, 2018

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ inquired about a statement included in the minutes
  regarding a request that the City send a letter to PVPUSD in support of maintaining the
  Equestrian Team at the high schools. MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that
  this matter will be brought before COUNCIL at the next meeting. Staff was directed to
  contact the School District to obtain additional information regarding this matter.

  MAYOR HUFF noted a correction to the minutes that Committee Member Patricia Harik
  should be listed as present.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE
  MINUTES OF MAY 19, 2018

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

I.  CITY CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING NOTES OF JUNE 6, 2018

  MAYOR HUFF reported that the City Celebration subcommittee came to a compromise
  that was acceptable all parties regarding the City Celebration and the Remember the
  Music Festival.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE CITY CELEBRATION
  SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING NOTES OF JUNE 6, 2018

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  COX COMMUNICATIONS PRESENTATION

  Meagan Collins and Kristen Camuglia reviewed a presentation on what Cox
  Communications is doing in the community including partnering with the community,
  investing in local infrastructure, innovation for the future and local updates including,
  Cox Communications’ Network Transform Project.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN urged Cox Communications to continue to further
  explore opportunities to provide wi-fi in the parks and expressed concern regarding
  service levels.

**  OTHER PUBLIC COMMENT

  Anna Chu, Palos Verdes Peninsula High School equestrian coach, addressed the City
  Council in support of the equestrian team and requested that the City Council send a letter
  to the PVPUSD Board of Directors encouraging the district to maintain the current
  equestrian teams.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 12, 2018
 7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 19-15: THE RESIDENCES AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY
  CLUB; PRODUCT B ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW REVISION

  Recommendation: That the City Council (1) open the Public Hearing; (2) take public
  testimony; (3) discuss the issues; (4) close the public hearing; and (5) affirm the Planning
  Commission’s approval of amendment PA-19-15, approving the incorporation of the
  proposed Product B plan types for the respective 31 lots.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and reviewed
  the proposed architectural designs.

  Peter Hemphill, Toll Brothers reviewed a presentation providing background and history
  on the company and explained how they will manage the project.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL provided an explanation as to why she called this project
  up specifically noting that there were very close votes during the Planning Commission’s
  consideration of the item and since Toll Brothers is new to the project she felt that the
  City Council should review the architectural designs. She commented that she is
  pleased with what is proposed, noting that the Planning Commission took into account
  that this development is a standalone development.

  Tim Scott, Planning Commissioner commented that his concern with the project when
  it was before the Planning Commission was that the architectural style did not reflect a
  ranch style character.
  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN, regarding the size of the homes,
  Planning Director Wahba commented that the homes are slightly larger than originally
  proposed but they still comply with the zoning regulations and are compatible with the
  neighborhood.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that from a policy standpoint, it is
  important to note that these designs are not typical Rolling Hills Estates ranch style
  homes and he is only supportive of the designs because of the Planning Commission’s
  justification that they are part of a stand-alone development where the architectural
  style is less reflective of a traditional ranch style property.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that he concurs with COUNCILMEMBER
  ZERUNYAN. He noted that the revised version of Plan 1C doesn’t seem consistent with
  the rest of the designs and feels that the original design is a better option.

  Planning Director Wahba commented that the revisions were made to address the
  Planning Commission’s concerns regarding mass but he too believes the original design
  may be a better option.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Hempill commented that they too
  prefer the original design for Plan 1C, but they will proceed in whichever direction the
  COUNCIL prefers.

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the revised design.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 12, 2018
   MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  MAYOR HUFF called for public comment. There were no members of the public present
  to comment on this item.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that based on the discussion regarding
  Plan 1C, he would be supportive of giving the builder the option to use either design for
  Plan 1C. MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL concurred.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AFFIRM THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S APPROVAL
  OF THE AMENDMENT TO PA-19-15; APPROVING THE INCORPORATION OF
  THE PROPOSED PROJECT B PLAN TYPES AS RECOMMENDED BUT ALLOWING
  EITHER OF THE TWO OPTIONS PROPOSED FOR PLAN 1C.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 05-18: ORDINANCE NO. 722 AMENDING AND RESTATING
  CHAPTER 17.56 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE RELATED TO
  ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS

  Recommendation: That the City Council (1) open the Public Hearing; (2) take public
  testimony; (3) discuss the issues; (4) introduce and conduct first reading of Ordinance
  No. 722 (amending and restating Chapter 17.56 of the RHEMC related to accessory
  dwelling units; and (5) close the public hearing and schedule second reading and
  adoption of the Ordinance No. 722.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material) noting that the
  ordinance includes a requirement that the second unit cannot be sold as a separate unit
  and the property owner must occupy one of the two dwelling units.

  Discussion ensued concerning the occupancy requirement, the requirement for a
  separate entrance if the unit on a second story, parking standards and garage
  conversions. Further discussion ensued concerning the impact second dwelling units
  will have on the City’s Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) numbers.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 12, 2018
   COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  MAYOR HUFF called for public comment.

  Tim Scott, Planning Commissioner asked if the ordinance has a specific requirement
  that the property owner occupy one of the units. Planning Director Wahba confirmed
  that is does. Further discussion ensued concerning the owner occupancy requirement
  and the need for enforcement on a case-by-case basis.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 722 FOR FIRST
  READING BY TITLE ONLY AND SCHEDULE SECOND READING FOR JUNE 26,
  2018.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Mayor Huff read Ordinance No. 722 by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – PROPOSITION 84 SANTA MONICA BAY CATCH
  BASIN INSERT PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU) by and among the cities of Rolling Hills Estates, Rancho Palos Verdes and Palos
  Verdes Estates related to the administration and cost sharing for implementing a
  Proposition 84 Grant for a Catch Basin Insert Project.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  commented that the City’s engineering consultant assisted with identifying the catch
  basins subject to this project noting that those chosen are tributary to Santa Monica
  Bay. Kathleen McGowan, McGowan Consulting commented that all of the catch basins
  in the commercial area and high-density residential areas have already been retrofit,
  leaving only single-family residential areas left to be retrofit.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JUNE 12, 2018
   MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT  THE  CITY  COUNCIL  APPROVE  THE MEMORANDUM  OF
  UNDERSTANDING BY AND AMONG THE CITIES OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES,
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES AND ROLLING HILLS ESTATES RELATED TO THE
  ADMINISTRATION AND COST SHARING FOR IMPLEMENTING A PROPOSITION
  84 GRANT FOR A CATCH BASIN INSERT PROJECT

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  REQUEST FOR TIME SCHEDULE ORDER FOR MACHADO LAKE NUTRIENT TMDL

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  Kathleen McGowan, McGowan Consulting reviewed the requirements for submitting the
  Time Schedule Order and the next steps in the process. In response to
  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN regarding what action steps are being taken, Ms.
  McGowan reviewed the specific steps outlined in the Time Schedule Order and the costs
  that have been committed to thus far.

  Discussion ensued concerning other options for complying with the requirements.
  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that it may be worthwhile to schedule a
  meeting with the neighboring cities to discuss other options. Further discussion ensued
  concerning the compliance requirements and reconsideration of the Machado Lake
  Nutrient TMDL.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT ON THE REQUEST
  FOR TIME SCHEDULE ORDER FOR MACHADO LAKE NUTRIENT TMDL

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

C.  MC GOWAN CONSULTING, LLC PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR MS4
  PERMIT CONSULTING SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a Professional Services Agreement with
  McGowan Consulting, LLC for MS4 Permit compliance assistance for FY 2018-19 in an
  amount not to exceed $90,760.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH MCGOWAN, LLC FOR MS4 PERMIT COMPLIANCE
  ASSISTANCE FOR FY 2018-19 IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $90,760

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

JUNE 12, 2018

COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ reported that the Chamber will be organizing another Wine Walk
